\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Post hoc and exploratory; the readouts hold for this grid and these seeds only and do not bound all content-blind transformations. The transformations choose items only by structural position, status enumeration and random seed (no gold, trap signatures, lexicons, validator results or item text), are applied to the frozen C2 artifacts and are rescored with the frozen scorer; values are means over seeds 1, 2, 3. S($p$) relabels (moves to unsupportedClaims) or deletes a fraction $p$ of supported-side items; R($q$) downgrades a fraction $q$ of supported requirements to partial evidence; X($r$) resets the decision-boundary fields to the repairer's constants and deletes a fraction $r$ of the interview-signal risk, human-review checklist and limitation items. ``S at C4's attrition / retention'': trap-failure rate on the S relabel curve, linearly interpolated at C4's supported items per case / C4's retention. S floor: trap-failure rate with the whole supported side removed (retention 0\%); over the three models 42/216 floor failures, of which 26 are decision-family cases (25 triggered by \texttt{anywhereSignatures}, 24 with the phrase in \texttt{interviewSignalRisks}), 14 requirement overclaims and 2 subjective-family extra-rule failures; the repairer's \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}fix\_\allowbreak{}requirements} downgraded a requirement status 0/0/0 times in the three runs. Non-decision families: the five families other than decision, with the curves and C4 coordinates recomputed on that subset; a model whose C2 and C4 differ by at most 2 cases there is not compared. Grid: configurations of $p \in \{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1\}$ with relabel or delete mode, $q \in \{0, 0.5, 1\}$ and $r \in \{0, 0.5, 1\}$. Trap-failure denominators: parseable risk cases; retention: parseable controls. \texttt{drop\_unsourced} relabels every supported-side item without a source ID.\par}
